mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers without equity decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation does not rise in response.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 98 for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or industrial production rebounds quickly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in HOUST and a decline in GDPC1 over the same month indicates a shift from durable goods demand to housing demand, which historically precedes a rotation into consumer discretionary weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rotation does not materialize.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling over two consecutive months signals a situation where employment expands but at lower wage growth, which historically precedes margin expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or wage growth accelerates unexpectedly.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2.0% for three consecutive months signals accommodative policy despite rising inflation, which historically supports equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.4% AND FEDFUNDS < 2.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or inflation expectations rise sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals rising household savings, which often precedes a reduction in consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or consumption does not decline.
